problem.text: LinearFP16.forward zero-filled its output before assigning the matrix product, doing initialization that successful multiplication does not need.

reasoning.text: Replacing zeros with empty avoids the explicit zero-fill while preserving allocation shape, device and subsequent multiplication. This is a performance optimization, not a reduction in output storage.

impact.text: Bias addition and restoration of the input's leading dimensions remain unchanged; correctness now explicitly relies on multiplication writing the output before bias reads it.

source_notes.text: The root quantized-inference entry was read. It establishes the original dense alternative and its cuBLAS alpha=1, beta=0 overwrite design.
Issue #39, “Gemma 3 architecture not in list?”, concerns architecture availability and later frontend/BOS discussion; it supplies no explicit connection to this allocation change.

limitations: No PyTorch or CUDA execution or performance measurement was performed. A scalar computation would not establish allocation cost or native output-write behavior.
The dtype expression now uses truthiness rather than an explicit None test. Actual torch.dtype truthiness was not tested; equivalence is conditional on supplied dtype objects being truthy.

chapters.title: Allocate dense linear output without zero initialization

claims.text: forward flattens input leading dimensions and allocates a two-dimensional output. Matching input/output dtypes select torch.matmul with out=y; differing dtypes select ext.hgemm. Neither selection changes in this commit.

The native alternative requires two-dimensional, shape-compatible half inputs and half or float output. Both cuBLAS branches pass alpha=1 and beta=0, selecting the product without accumulation of previous output contents. This existing overwrite contract supplies the precondition for removing zero initialization.

Dtype selection changes from first_not_none(out_dtype, self.out_dtype, torch.half) to an or chain. The helper selected the first non-None value; the replacement selects the first truthy value, retaining the same priority for truthy dtype values and falling back to half.

annotation.summary: LinearFP16 replaces zero-filled output allocation with empty allocation and simplifies dtype selection. Existing multiplication paths supply overwrite semantics; speedup and numerical behavior were not measured.
